summary: Updates RFC 3405 by removing references to the IETF tree from the procedure for getting a URI scheme added to the URI.ARPA zone. It is a small process change to registration rules, published as a Best Current Practice.

plainLanguage.summary: This Best Current Practice updates the rules for adding URI schemes to URI.ARPA. It removes a requirement to use an IETF URI tree that was no longer part of the current registration process.

questions: how to register a uri scheme in uri.arpa
what did rfc 8958 change in rfc 3405
what is the ietf tree for uri schemes
which uri schemes can be added to uri.arpa
subtitle: Updated registration rules remove a requirement to use a discontinued URI scheme tree.

tldr.problem: RFC 3405 required URI.ARPA registrations to come from the IETF URI tree, but the tree-based process had been discontinued.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC removes that requirement and requires every URI.ARPA registration to use a permanently registered URI scheme.
tldr.outcome: The updated instructions align URI.ARPA registration with the process in BCP 35. RFC 8958 is a Best Current Practice that updates RFC 3405.

today: RFC 8958 is a Best Current Practice that updates RFC 3405. The unit metadata lists no RFC that updates or obsoletes RFC 8958.

sections.title: Why the URI.ARPA Rule Changed
sections.content:
Part Five of the Dynamic Delegation Discovery System, RFC 3405, describes registrations in URI.ARPA and required them to be in the IETF tree of URI registrations.

URI scheme name trees were defined in RFC 2717 and later discontinued. The current registration process in BCP 35 therefore had no way to satisfy the old requirement.
sections.plainLanguage: The old URI.ARPA rule required a registration path that no longer existed. This RFC changes the rule to use the current process.

sections.title: The New Registration Requirement
sections.content: RFC 8958 removes RFC 3405's requirement that URI.ARPA registrations come from the IETF URI tree. It replaces that requirement with a rule that all URI.ARPA registrations MUST be for URI schemes with permanent registrations, as described in BCP 35 (RFC 7595).
sections.plainLanguage: A URI.ARPA entry must now use a URI scheme that has a permanent registration under the current guidelines.

sections.title: Instructions to IANA
sections.content: The RFC states that the entire document is updated instructions to IANA. Its change to the registration requirement is the instruction.
sections.plainLanguage: IANA should apply the new permanent-registration requirement when handling URI.ARPA registrations.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: This update does not change the security considerations in RFC 3405. The RFC makes a registration-procedure change and leaves the earlier security guidance in place.
sections.plainLanguage: The registration-rule change does not alter RFC 3405's security considerations.
